description: Held-out. Repurpose a finished club blog post into a thread. Figures with units survive, the negative finding (site visits not reduced) stays, the cause of the improvement stays hedged (a mild winter may explain some or all of the gap) together with the one-winter, small-sample limit, nothing is added (no figures, names, links, endorsement), the canonical link is kept, and the thread is restructured rather than pasted.
prompt: Turn the write-up in writeup.md into a thread for Bluesky. Save the thread to out/thread.md. No hashtags.

files.writeup.md:
# We put timers on our hive feeders. More colonies came through winter.

Canonical: https://example.org/marrowby/feeder-timers

By Odalys Prieto, Marrowby Bee Club

Last autumn the club fed its hives by hand. Someone had to visit each site every few days to top up the syrup. This year we fitted battery timers to the feeders on 12 hives across 3 apiary sites, so the syrup went out on a fixed schedule from 6 October to 24 November. Each timer cost 14 pounds.

We counted colonies on 15 March. 11 of the 12 timer-fed colonies were alive. The winter before, with hand feeding, 9 of 12 colonies on the same sites were alive. The timers did not reduce the number of site visits, because we still checked every hive for disease every two weeks.

We think the schedule helped, but we cannot be sure of it. This winter was milder than the one before, and the mild weather may explain some or all of the difference. We have one winter of data and 12 colonies in each group, so a gap of two colonies is small.

If you try timers on your own hives, count your colonies in March and compare them with last year before you decide.

checks.note: figures and the 'did not reduce site visits' negation must survive; hedge words may change, the mild-winter hedge is checked below
thread numbering is allowed; no other figure or link

checks.pattern: (?is)mild\w*[^\n]{0,160}\b(?:may|might|could|possibly|some or all|cannot rule|can't rule|not sure|unclear|partly|can't say|cannot say|can't tell|cannot tell|can't be sure|cannot be sure|not proof)\b|\b(?:may|might|could|possibly|some or all|cannot rule|can't rule|not sure|unclear|partly|can't say|cannot say|can't tell|cannot tell|can't be sure|cannot be sure|not proof)\b[^\n]{0,160}mild
checks.note: the mild-winter explanation stays hedged, in whichever hedge word. The hedge may sit in the next sentence of the same post ('This winter was milder. Weather may explain...') or say the cause cannot be told; the earlier pattern needed it in the same sentence and without 'can't say'
the one-winter limit is carried over
the post says the authors cannot be sure; the thread must not turn the finding into a proven cause

the finding that timers did not reduce site visits is carried over with its negation. This replaces the 'not' count in the generic preserves check (see allow_lost there), which also counted 'cannot be sure' and so failed threads that restate that caution as 'may explain' or 'can't say'
more than one post, shorter than the source
